index_title: Finite-index packets, minimal cuts and exact-kernel normalization
scope: Preparation for OTHER Lean projects. All eight numbered results of finite_packets.tex, four auxiliary equations and the twin-cell example are expanded. General index algebra, triangle-law packet geometry, elementary square regularization, source-preserving normalization and thin-group transport are separated. No SAP, NR2, selectors or owner groupoid is introduced.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Actual quotient-orbital algebra is weaker than full quotient-source inheritance; thin finite packets need not be free of nonidentity exact kernels.

assumptions.name: Actual symmetric original source
assumptions.statement: An inhabited transitive homogeneous complete finite symmetric binary original source, possibly finite. Logical equality is separate from the finite diversity palette. All relations are actual original automorphism-invariant pair-orbital unions. Same-sort invariant endorelations commute, without CCO or SAP.

assumptions.name: Original AP and semantic homomorphic CCO
assumptions.statement: The actual original age has AP and semantic homomorphic CCO. Used through I01 triangle fullness and I02 exact quotient-source inheritance. Never infer source inheritance for arbitrary nonexact kernels.

assumptions.name: Elementary cardinal and finite combinatorics
assumptions.statement: Finite choices, finite-set counting, powers in a finite palette, finite pigeonhole, finite groups and their elementary abelian identification. Relative indices are cardinalities of actual class quotients, possibly infinite; a natural-number cardinal is used only after proving finiteness. A sufficient finite triangle Ramsey bound is expanded internally.

assumptions.name: Optional thin finite bottom
assumptions.statement: For the translation-group branch all atomic orbitals contained in the greatest finite-class invariant equivalence F are thin. This does not imply absence of nonidentity finite-class exact kernels.

assumptions.name: Countable original source for the current inheritance provider
assumptions.statement: For C13/C24/C25 retain the pinned exact-quotient source provider's countability premise. Initial M is countable and each actual quotient is countable as an image. The elementary index, regularizer and thin-group branches do not require countability; no uncountable joint-lifting extension is claimed.

imports.name: lem:cco-triangle-fullness
imports.statement: Original complete-diagram triangle fullness follows from age AP and original semantic homomorphic CCO. Loop arguments consume only this triangle law, not SAP or arbitrary imaginary inheritance.

imports.name: thm:exact-sorts-source
imports.statement: For the COUNTABLE current original source, an actual quotient by an original FULL RAW exact invariant equivalence is again homogeneous, transitive, symmetric, triangle-defined AP and semantic-homomorphic-CCO in its actual binary orbital language. No arbitrary nonexact quotient is included.

imports.name: lem:foundational-orbital-pullback
imports.statement: For actual equivariant quotient maps of a transitive group action, the pullback of the orbital of a quotient pair is kernel;old orbital;kernel. This elementary group-action law does not require quotient homogeneity, SAP, CCO or exactness.

imports.name: lem:rh-evenwalk
imports.statement: Even connectivity of a symmetric diversity atom is one actual positive even RAW word profile. If the atom is looped, even connectivity equals full Gamma connectivity. No CCO or SAP is needed for this elementary represented-word law.

definitions.name: Full invariant-equivalence lattice
definitions.statement: All original invariant equivalences on the real sort, ordered by inclusion; actual Top and Id, meets by intersection and joins by represented commuting composition.

definitions.name: Actual relative class index
definitions.statement: For J<=K, [K:J] is the uniform cardinality of J-classes contained in one K-class. Uniformity follows from original transitivity; finite claims carry a finiteness guard.

definitions.name: Finite-index closure Sigma and F
definitions.statement: Sigma(J) is the greatest K>=J with finite [K:J]; C03 constructs it. F=Sigma(Id) is the greatest finite-class original equivalence, not necessarily exact.

definitions.name: Looped atoms and packet core
definitions.statement: A looped DIVERSITY atom has an actual monochromatic triangle. Gamma(a) is its full connectivity equivalence. Kappa(J) is the join of Gamma(a) for looped a<=J; empty join is actual Id.

definitions.name: Minimal infinite cut and finite part H
definitions.statement: When the source is infinite, E is inclusion-minimal among original equivalences with infinite classes and H=E meet F. E may be Top, and no E<Sigma(E) condition is imposed.

definitions.name: Finite square regularizer H0
definitions.statement: For all diversity atoms a_i<=F set P=product a_i², with empty product Id, and let H0 be a stabilized positive power of P. Identity is real equality, not a diversity letter.

definitions.name: Actual quotient orbitals
definitions.statement: On actual classes M/K use the original group action; each quotient pair orbital has pullback K;a;K. A pullback can contain several old atoms and is not itself declared an old single atom.

definitions.name: Thin atom and unique-neighbour permutation
definitions.statement: A thin atomic relation has exactly one neighbour at every point; symmetry makes its unique-neighbour map an involution. Equality is allowed as the neutral thin relation.

definitions.name: Thin translation group and subgroup relation
definitions.statement: Thin atoms within F, including equality, form a finite group by represented composition. A subgroup H corresponds to the union of its thin orbital graphs, not a choice of packet origins.

definitions.name: Palette rank for normalization
definitions.statement: The nonnegative integer number of diversity orbitals in the CURRENT actual quotient source. Every nonidentity quotient kernel removes at least one diversity orbital into quotient equality.

claims.name: Elementary symmetric lattice calculus
claims.statement: Pair-orbital uniformity makes invariant endorelations symmetric, so represented products commute. Composition of commuting invariant equivalences is their full join; the full lattice is finite, not presumed distributive.

claims.name: Index transposition and finite tower bounds
claims.statement: For commuting equivalences, map actual classes in one class into classes of their join; uniform bijections give [A join B:B]=[A:A meet B]. For J<=L<=K with finite [K:J], all intermediate indices are finite and [K:J]=[K:L][L:J]. Restriction gives [E meet K:E meet J]<=[K:J]. No Nat.card argument on an unproved infinite type is used.

claims.name: Existence and closure properties of Sigma
claims.statement: If K1,K2>=J have finite relative index, [K1 join K2:J] <=[K1:J][K2:J]. Finite joining all finite-index coarsenings constructs Sigma(J), with J<=Sigma(J), finite index and idempotence. If J<=K has finite index then Sigma(J)=Sigma(K). In particular F exists with finite classes.

claims.name: Elementary finite triangle Ramsey
claims.statement: For k>=1 let f_k(0)=1 and f_k(t+1)=k f_k(t)+1. In a k-coloured complete graph on f_k(k+1) points, select k+1 monochromatic-outgoing pivots and a final point; two pivot colours agree and supply a monochromatic triangle. No infinite Ramsey theorem is imported.

claims.name: Relative loop criterion
claims.statement: For J<=K, a looped diversity atom in K outside J gives arbitrarily many distinct J-classes in one K-class by triangle-full monochromatic cliques. Conversely infinitely many J-classes in a K-class supply just the finite Ramsey number of representatives, and hence a looped atom outside J. Thus [K:J] finite iff no such atom exists.

claims.name: Core monotonicity and finite refinement
claims.statement: Kappa(J)<=J; cores are monotone. Every looped atom in J is contained in its core, so [J:kappa(J)] is finite by the loop criterion. If J<=K has finite index they have the same looped atoms and the same core.

claims.name: Core and member have the same closure
claims.statement: The finite-index extension kappa(J)<=J implies Sigma(kappa(J))=Sigma(J), and kappa(J)=kappa(Sigma(J)). Same-Sigma equivalences have the same core.

claims.name: Entire packet is its closed interval
claims.statement: Sigma(L)=Sigma(J) iff kappa(J)<=L<=Sigma(J). For the converse [Sigma(J):kappa(J)] is finite; finite index through L gives both Sigma(J)<=Sigma(L) and Sigma(L)<=Sigma(kappa(J))=Sigma(J). No distributivity or exactness of Sigma endpoints is used.

claims.name: Loop connectivity is a positive atomic word
claims.statement: For a looped diversity atom, a<=a² and Id<=a². Its even powers increase and stabilize in the finite actual palette to its connectivity equivalence Gamma(a), a positive RAW word profile. This is the looped instance of the elementary even-walk provider.

claims.name: Core word exactness with the identity boundary
claims.statement: Each nontrivial kappa(J) is a finite nonempty join/product of the positive word profiles Gamma(a) of its looped atoms, hence one positive atomic word and FULL RAW exact. The empty family yields Id, represented by the actual empty word, not a positive diversity identity.

claims.name: Elementary geometry below a minimal infinite cut
claims.statement: Every proper original J<E has finite classes and lies in H=E meet F, giving [Id,E]=[Id,H] union {E}. E admits no proper finite-index refinement. A strict finite-index interval J<K<=E has K<=H. This uses minimality and finite-class F, not CCO or exact quotient geometry.

claims.name: Minimal cut equals its exact core
claims.statement: Kappa(E)<=E has finite relative index. Its classes cannot be finite because E is infinite; minimality gives E=kappa(E), which is nonidentity and word exact by C10.

claims.name: Actual minimal-cut quotient inherits the full source
claims.statement: Apply the exact quotient-source provider to the actual exact kernel E from C12. This is the separate provider for homogeneous/triangle/AP/CCO properties of M/E; elementary index identities alone do not imply it.

claims.name: Finite restriction across the cut
claims.statement: Put I=E meet J and L=E meet K for J<=K of finite index. The injection of I-classes into J-classes inside a K-class gives finite [L:I]. If I<L, then L cannot equal E (otherwise a forbidden proper finite-index refinement), hence L<=H.

claims.name: Modular path rerouting
claims.statement: For ANY invariant E and J<=K, K meet (E join J)=J join (E meet K), by commuting represented-product witnesses. No minimal-cut hypothesis or full-lattice distributivity is used.

claims.name: Crossing meet can replace E by H
claims.statement: For the minimal infinite cut and finite [K:J], use C14 and C15 to get K meet (E join J)=K meet (H join J). Handle E meet J=E meet K separately from the strict case.

claims.name: General actual finite-index factorization
claims.statement: For ANY E and J<=K of finite index, the actual class projection has kernel D=K meet (E join J). It is onto by permutability; fibres have size [E meet K:E meet J]. Tower and two class transpositions give [K:J]=[E join K:E join J][E meet K:E meet J], with finite factors. Minimality and H are unnecessary for this factorization.

claims.name: Sigma crossing identity
claims.statement: F join J has finite relative index over J, so F<=Sigma(J). Insert K=Sigma(J) into C16 to obtain Sigma(J) meet (E join J)=J join H. This assertion retains minimality of E.

claims.name: Finite exact square kernel construction
claims.statement: Every actual symmetric atom a_i<=F has Id<=a_i². The product P of its diversity squares is invariant, symmetric, reflexive and lies in F; its powers increase and stabilize to H0=P^n with H0²=H0. Hence H0 is finite-class exact, H0<=F and a_i²<=H0. The empty diversity list gives H0=Id via the empty word.

claims.name: Actual quotient atom pullbacks
claims.statement: For H0 and each old atom a_i<=F INCLUDING actual Id, beyond the diversity list D06, H0;a_i;H0 is the pullback of one actual quotient pair orbital, by I03; it may contain many old atoms. Every quotient orbital inside F/H0 arises this way. This uses only the ambient group action and does not assert quotient source inheritance.

claims.name: The finite quotient packet has thin atoms
claims.statement: Its orbital b has square equal to quotient equality since its pullback square is H0;a_i²;H0=H0. Nonempty symmetric b is serial by transitivity, and b²=Id forces uniqueness of neighbours; this includes the neutral quotient diagonal.

claims.name: Thin and nonthin initial branches
claims.statement: If all old atoms within F are thin then each square is Id and the construction returns H0=Id. If some atom is nonthin, two distinct neighbours of one point yield a nonidentity output in a_i²<=H0, so H0>Id. Neither statement says thin F is exact-kernel-free.

claims.name: Nonidentity quotients strictly lower the palette
claims.statement: For a nonidentity invariant kernel K the quotient pair-orbital partition is obtained by grouping old pair orbitals. Quotient equality contains old identity and at least one old diversity atom. Hence the number of quotient diversity orbitals is strictly smaller. No exactness or quotient homogeneity is needed for the partition/count assertion.

claims.name: Finite source-preserving exact normalization
claims.statement: While a nonidentity finite-class exact kernel exists in the current source, quotient by it. I02 preserves all source properties, C23 strictly decreases the current palette, so finite induction gives a chain ending with no such kernel. Chain length zero is allowed; use the CURRENT palette at each step.

claims.name: Terminal exact-kernel-free source has thin F
claims.statement: If a terminal F-atom were nonthin, C22 would construct a nonidentity finite-class exact H0, contradiction. Thus all its F-atoms are thin. The converse is false and is not used.

claims.name: Thin maps are equivariant involutions
claims.statement: Under the optional thin-F hypothesis every atom below F gives a globally defined unique-neighbour involution t_g, commuting with the original automorphism action by uniqueness. Equality gives the identity map. Automorphism of the structure itself is proved later.

claims.name: Finite elementary abelian group regular on packets
claims.statement: Compositions of the equivariant thin permutations are invariant functional relations in F; atomic seriality forces exactly one atom. They form a finite group all of whose elements square to identity, hence elementary abelian, and its action on each F-class is free and transitive. No packet origin is chosen.

claims.name: Single-atom colour transport and central automorphisms
claims.statement: The equivariant endpoint switch sends one actual old pair orbital bijectively to another, so q_g;a is one atom g·a. Commutation supplies the second endpoint rule and col(t_g x,t_h y)=(g+h)·col(x,y), INCLUDING equality. Setting h=g proves each t_g is an original automorphism; the established equivariance makes it central. This is an action on atoms, not permission to permute colours arbitrarily.

claims.name: Lower interval is a subgroup lattice plus cut
claims.statement: Under thin F, an invariant relation below F is an equivalence precisely when the chosen thin-atom subset is a subgroup. Thus H=E meet F is a subgroup and [Id,E] is order-isomorphic to Sub(H) with the additional greatest element E, using the elementary minimal-cut interval. No arbitrary imaginary quotient action or origin compatibility follows.

claims.name: Twin-cell source has homogeneous AP and CCO age
claims.statement: For I×J×{0,1} with colours t inside cells and r,c,b depending only on coordinate equality, finite isomorphisms extend via coordinate permutations and independent cell flips. Triangle constraints enforce two coordinate equivalences and at most two points per cell. Partial-coordinate inconsistency gives a bad specified simple cycle; remaining t-constraints require a bipartite graph in a forced cell, with odd t-cycles as obstructions. Thus the infinite source has semantic CCO.

claims.name: Thin F can still be a nontrivial finite exact kernel
claims.statement: In the twin-cell source F=Id union t has thin atoms and square regularizer H0=Id, yet r² and c² are the two coordinate equivalences, so F=r² meet c² is nonidentity RAW exact. For E=the row equivalence, E meet c²=F and each realised conditional c-fibre over a fixed target row owner has size two. Quotienting F lowers the palette; thinness alone does not reach normalization.

review.method: Independent reviews of lattice/crossing and regularization/thin-group branches, parent synthesis and finite controls. No human or Lean certification.
review.remaining: Receiving projects must implement actual finite class indices, quotient source contracts and all proofs. No arbitrary nonexact quotient or owner-groupoid compatibility theorem follows.

overview_mermaid: E["Actual invariant relation algebra"] --> I["Finite index and Sigma"]
R["Finite triangle Ramsey"] --> L["Relative loop criterion"]
overview_notes: General crossing index factorization does not need minimality, CCO or full-lattice distributivity.
Square regularization and thin-group transport do not need CCO; normalization of the source does.
Thin F and absence of nonidentity finite-class exact kernels are distinct conditions.
